gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: While I ___ the report yesterday, my laptop battery died.
gaps.hint: the battery died interrupted the writing
gaps.explanation: The dying battery interrupted the ongoing writing, so the past continuous fits: was writing.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ for over two hours.
gaps.hint: for over two hours up to now
gaps.explanation: A duration continuing up to the present moment takes the present perfect continuous: have been chatting.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ discussing one agenda item for an hour.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour' and still relevant — present perfect continuous.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.
